threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to stand on the left side of the escalators at Dalston Junction. Everyone knows it’s all about the right side here.
Heard a couple arguing about a missing shoe on the N109 last night. Turns out, she threw it out the window at some guy on a bike.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full suit riding his bike with a giant inflatable flamingo under his arm to the canal. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Neukölln, you can find cafes that serve traditional Turkish breakfast alongside vegan brunch, all while the smell of fresh simit wafts through the air.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals know to avoid 16th Street BART on weekdays after 5 PM; it’s like a rush hour Bermuda Triangle for delays and lost patience.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 this morning, and it stopped for 10 minutes to let a guy get his sax out of a bush. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can stroll into any bar and get a proper vermut, but only locals know the hidden gems that serve it on tap with the right olives.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle to navigate the Gràcia's winding streets; they often look down at their phones, confused, while locals breeze by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look in shock when the bus doesn’t stop on the red light at Kingsland Road. Everyone else just conducts business as usual.
Last night, a couple argued over their takeaway on the N37; she threw chips at him as the bus went past the snazzy new library. Hilarious.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw three kids selling handmade lemonade outside the U-Bahn entrance, laughing as they mimicked the ticket machines.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you spot a guy in a suit enthusiastically tango dancing with a stranger on the U-Bahn platform at 7 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they dodge the BART rats like they’re part of the daily commute. Tourists just stare.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo sprinting to catch the Muni while juggling a giant teddy bear. Classic Tenderloin chaos, only in this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about the Gaudí, but the real magic is in the small, family-run bakeries where the local pastisseria has been the same for decades.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them struggling with paella etiquette, often assuming it's a one-dish meal instead of a communal feast. It's the little things.
